sentences.text: The femur of Meroktenos is very compact with a robusticity index of 2.09.
This animal possesses a remarkably high relative transverse width of the femur for its small size.
The holotype specimen MNHN.F.LES 16 consists of a right femur, part of the right ilium, a vertebral neural arch, a left pubic bone, and a second right metatarsal.
The genus name Meroktenos combines the ancient Greek words for "thigh" and "beast".
Researchers suggest that the unusual femoral proportions of Meroktenos must have served a function different from supporting giant body weight, as the animal was likely not a giant.
The type specimen of Meroktenos was discovered in 1959 by François Ellenberger, Paul Ellenberger, Jean Fabre, and Leonard Ginsburg south of the village of Thabana Morena.
Meroktenos was established as a separate genus in 2016 by Claire Peyre de Fabrègues and Ronan Allain.
In 2016, Meroktenos was classified within the Sauropodomorpha at a basal position.
Meroktenos is classified as an animal in the phylum Chordata, class Sauropsida, order Saurischia, and suborder Sauropodomorpha.
Meroktenos lived during the Late Triassic period in what is now Lesotho.
Meroktenos thabanensis lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 216 to 201 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
Meroktenos lived from the Norian to the Rhaetian stages, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
